subject: Cluster boarding: network handoff & PV ownership (readout)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@valence-tech.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@valence-tech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cluster boarding: network handoff & PV ownership (readout)

Thanks for the time on the intake call this morning. I wanted to capture the immediate action items and align on who owns which pieces so we can get your private cluster into our onboarding sprint next week.

High-level asks (can you confirm by EOD?):
- Network path: do you have a designated eBGP peer for cross-site routing or will we use static routes via the customer edge?
- Egress requirements: any corporate egress IPs we should reserve for outbound telemetry?
- Airgapped requirement: you mentioned limited internet egress for model pulls — confirm if mirror registry will be provided.
- PV ownership and CSI: who on Valence will be responsible for installing the CSI driver and ensuring KMS access for encryption keys?

Attachment: valence_nwp_diagram.png (network diagram you shared), and a draft preflight checklist.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Karthik will produce a node-pool sizing sketch and PV-binding approach for transactional workloads.
- Laura will validate our preflight checklist against your internal Ops playbook.
- Marissa (me) will coordinate timeline and procurement questions with procurement if reserved capacity is needed.

Can you confirm the owner for CSI/KMS and whether the cluster will be able to reach our S3-compatible mirror during bootstrap?

Thanks — short bullets are perfect.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf

Subject: Re: Cluster boarding: network handoff & PV ownership (readout)

Thanks Marissa — solid summary. Quick clarifications: 
- We'll be on static routes to the CE (no BGP for this site).
- Egress: we can reserve two IPs (one for telemetry, one for model pull). I'll send the IPs after I confirm with networking.
- Airgap: yes, we'll provide a registry mirror; Ops will host it on premise.
- CSI/KMS: Valence Ops will install the CSI driver, but we need Redwood's guidance on the exact driver version and CSI parameters for delayed binding. We will own the KMS keys (HSM-backed).

Also: is there a recommended PVC reclaim policy you prefer for ephemeral GPU-backed workloads? We want to avoid accidental deletes during preemptible scheduling.

Oliver

On Wed, Apr 21, 2027 at 11:05 AM Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@valence-tech.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — solid summary. Quick clarifications: 
> - We'll be on static routes to the CE (no BGP for this site).
> - Egress: we can reserve two IPs (one for telemetry, one for model pull). I'll send the IPs after I confirm with networking.
> - Airgap: yes, we'll provide a registry mirror; Ops will host it on premise.
> - CSI/KMS: Valence Ops will install the CSI driver, but we need Redwood's guidance on the exact driver version and CSI parameters for delayed binding. We will own the KMS keys (HSM-backed).
> 
> Also: is there a recommended PVC reclaim policy you prefer for ephemeral GPU-backed workloads? We want to avoid accidental deletes during preemptible scheduling.

Thanks — answering inline below and adding Karthik for implementation details.
- Static routes is fine; we'll include instructions for NAT and health-check probes for control-plane egress.
- Once you share IPs we'll plug them into our firewall template and telemetry whitelist.
- Registry mirror: we can support your mirror for the initial bootstrap (we'll provide the image list and digest pins to pre-populate).
- CSI/KMS: Redwood recommends CSI driver v4.2.x for our installer at this time; we'll provide a small helm values snippet to enforce delayed binding (StorageClass: volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer).
- PVC reclaim: for GPU-ephemeral we recommend Recycle -> Retain? For long-lived artifacts use Retain with a garbage collection job; for scratch workloads set ReclaimPolicy: Delete but enforce a lifecycle TTL via an operator. Karthik, can you draft the operator/gc suggestion?

I'll attach a short CSV with suggested PV annotations (pv-policy-diff.csv) and the network diagram we discussed.

—
Marissa

Attachments: pv-policy-diff.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Tan <oliver.tan@valence-tech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cluster boarding: network handoff & PV ownership (readout)

Folks — posting the operational readout and concrete config snippets you asked for. Summary of decisions and actions for sprint kickoff next Monday: 

1) Node pools (initial):
- control-plane (3x m6.large-equivalent) - redundant, no GPU, tolerations for control-plane-only daemons.
- gpu-worker (6x a100-equivalent) - tainted gpu=true:NoSchedule; recommended local NVMe for model cache (ephemeral).
- general-worker (4x r5-like) - for services, infra, sidecars.

2) Storage and PV strategy:
- Transactional model checkpoints -> RWO PVs with StorageClass 'redwood-fast-ssd' (WaitForFirstConsumer).
- Large archival blobs -> object-store (S3-compatible) mounted via sidecar for streaming; avoid binding big blockstore PVs where possible.
- Reclaim policy: set Retain for transactional PVs that represent checkpoints; scratch GPUs use Delete + lifecycle operator that prunes after 48h idle.

3) CSI/KMS
- We'll supply helm values for CSI v4.2.1 and a sample SecretProviderClass for your HSM-wrapped keys. Since Valence owns keys, Redwood will request a short-lived service principal with PKCS#11 access to fetch encryption keys during PV provisioning.

4) Network / egress / firewall
- Static routes accepted. We need the two IPs for telemetry/model-pull. We'll add explicit iptables rules in the bootstrap script and a NetworkPolicy template for control-plane egress: allow TCP 443 to the three whitelisted IPs, allow NTP, DNS to internal resolvers only.

5) Acceptance tests (what we'll run during onboarding):
- Image pull from your mirror and checksum verification for the pinned images.
- PV bind/unbind for volumeBindingMode tests across node pools.
- Model load & inference smoke test on GPU worker to validate steady-state latency.

6) Ops handoff items (owners):
- Valence: provide mirror registry endpoint + two egress IPs (Oliver).
- Valence: install CSI driver (Priya) — follow our helm values; Redwood will validate.
- Redwood: supply key-fetch sample and preflight checklist (Marissa/Laura).

I'll drop the NetworkPolicy and StorageClass stubs into the Drive folder and create the HubSpot task under deal RDW-7892. If you can confirm the egress IPs by Monday morning we'll lock the kickoff window.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
